core_obligations: Set up the measurement of the level: fix a uniformizer pi of A, take w in B and P in B[t] from the preparation lemma applied to B, put e_1 equal to the order of w so that w and pi^{e_1} are associates in B, choose z in M generating M over L with xi = P(z) in K and n with pi^n xi in B, so that l = n/e_1 (proof lines 35183-35188).

Extract the two congruences that make P behave like the polynomial z^p - z inside the truncated quotient: P(z) is congruent to z^p - z modulo pi^{-n + e_1}B for every z with pi^{-n}P(z) in B, and xi_1 + xi_2 + w^p xi_1 xi_2 is congruent to xi_1 + xi_2 modulo pi^{-2n + p e_1}B for xi_1, xi_2 in pi^{-n}B; note that n - e_1 corresponds to l - 1 and that -2n + p e_1 corresponds to -(2l - p)e_1, and set m = n - e_1 max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) (proof lines 35190-35209).

Lift compatible residue-field representatives modulo pi^m for the residue field of A and the residue field of B, lift the second one to a map of sets from the residue field of B to B, and expand xi as a finite sum of sigma(lambda_i) pi^{-i} over i = n down to n - m + 1 plus an error term in pi^{-n + m}B; split the index set into the set I of indices whose coefficient lies in the residue field of A and the set J of the remaining ones (proof lines 35211-35232).

Treat the case where J is empty: use the chosen lift to write xi = pi^{-n}a + pi^{-n + m}b with a in A; if p divides n, write a = a_0^p + pi a_1 using perfectness of the residue field of A, put z_1 = -pi^{-n/p} a_0, observe that z + z_1 + w z z_1 still generates M over L and that the value of P there is congruent to xi + z_1^p - z_1 modulo pi^{-n + m}B, contradicting the minimality of n; conclude that p does not divide n (proof lines 35234-35255).

Finish the case where J is empty: build the degree p extension K_1 of K by the equation P(y) = -pi^{-n}a, which the dictionary lemma makes separable and totally ramified with respect to A, form L_1 = L tensor K_1 and M_1 = M tensor K_1, and show that either the first alternative of the statement holds, or M_1/L_1 is a field extension generated by z + y + w z y whose value under P is congruent to xi - pi^{-n}a modulo pi^{-n + m}B_1, hence zero, so that the level of M_1/L_1 is at most max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) (proof lines 35255-35280).

In the general case, first shrink J by the p-power-orbit move: if j' = p^r j with r positive, change z into z + z_1 + w z z_1 with the explicit z_1 = -sigma(lambda_j) pi^{-j} - sigma(lambda_j^p) pi^{-pj} - ... - sigma(lambda_j^{p^{r-1}}) pi^{-p^{r-1}j}, which makes the new coefficient at j vanish, leaves all other coefficients unchanged, and hence lets one assume by induction on the size of J that no two elements of J differ by a power of p (proof lines 35282-35309).

Final step: write each lambda_j as mu_j^{p^{r_j}} with mu_j not a p-th power, take the unique j for which j p^{-r_j} is maximal, choose r larger than every r_j + 1 and large enough that j p^{r - r_j} exceeds n for all j in J, let K_1 over K be the degree p^r extension defined by extracting a p^r-th root of pi with pi' a uniformizer of the corresponding discrete valuation ring A_1, carry out the computation in the integral closure B_1, correct z by the explicit z_1 built from the x_i and the sigma(mu_j), and read off from the resulting congruence that the level of M_1/L_1 is less than max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) or that M_1/L_1 falls into the third case of the dictionary lemma, which finishes the proof (proof lines 35311-35366).
proof_roadmap: Measure the level through the normal form of the extension: fix pi, take w and P from the preparation lemma, put e_1 = ord_B(w), choose z generating M over L with xi = P(z) in K and n with pi^n xi in B, so that l = n/e_1 (proof lines 35183-35188).

Replace the polynomial P by z^p - z modulo the two error terms, namely pi^{-n + e_1}B in the value and pi^{-2n + p e_1}B in the multiplicative correction law, and choose m so that the target level max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) is exactly the exponent reached by these errors (proof lines 35190-35209).
Lift residue-field representatives and expand xi in pi^{-n}B modulo pi^{-n + m}B, splitting the coefficients into those in the residue field of A and those outside it (proof lines 35211-35232).

When all coefficients lie in the residue field of A, either derive a contradiction with the minimality of n or build an explicit degree p extension of K and show that the base-changed extension already has level at most max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) (proof lines 35234-35280).

Otherwise remove first all pairs of indices related by a power of p, then apply a degree p^r base change obtained by extracting a p^r-th root of a uniformizer and recompute the expansion in the integral closure to read off the new level (proof lines 35282-35366).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the level-lowering step of the elimination-of-ramification argument: for discrete valuation rings A contained in B contained in C with fraction fields K contained in L contained in M, with A of mixed characteristic (0, p), A in B weakly unramified, B containing a primitive p-th root of 1 and the residue field of A equal to the intersection of the p-power residue fields of B, a degree p extension M/L of positive finite level l can be brought to level at most max(0, l - 1, 2l - p) after a finite separable base change of K that is totally ramified with respect to A, unless that base change is already a weak solution (statement lines 35166-35179). The argument is not a citation: it first converts the polynomial presenting M/L into the polynomial z^p - z modulo two explicitly computed error terms, one for the value and one for the multiplicative correction law, and chooses the exponent m so that those errors land exactly on the target level (proof lines 35190-35209). The core is an induction on the number of coefficients of xi that lie outside the residue field of A: pairs of indices related by a power of p are removed by an explicit correction of the generating element, and in the remaining case a base change of degree p^r obtained by extracting a p^r-th root of a uniformizer is performed and the computation is redone in the integral closure, so that the new level is read off from an expansion rather than from a general principle (proof lines 35282-35366). The degenerate case in which all coefficients lie in the residue field of A is closed by a contradiction with the minimality of n, using that the residue field of A is perfect, and then by an explicit degree p extension of K (proof lines 35234-35280); the level invariant, the p-power-orbit reduction and the p^r base change together are what put this beyond routine technique.

Public 423 is the statement that the level-lowering lemma is a tool for: it is the elimination-of-ramification conclusion for essentially finite-type valuation-ring extensions, proved further down the same chapter at source lines 35960-36069, and it is not a corollary of the present lemma in either direction. The present lemma is an auxiliary result with its own hypotheses (weakly unramified A in B, a primitive p-th root of 1 in B, the intersection condition on residue fields) and its own conclusion about the level after a base change, and the text that uses it sits at source lines 35496-35500, outside the counted spans of both cards.
